title: The Unjust King and the Pilgrim Prince

keywords: the unjust king and the pilgrim prince
full_text:
In the ancient kingdom of Sind reigned a tyrannical monarch who extorted heavy taxes from the peasantry, confiscated the estates of merchants, and cast into prison any citizen who spoke of justice.

One afternoon, a young pilgrim dressed in a simple woollen tunic entered the royal audience hall, leaning upon an ebony walking staff. Despite his humble attire, his countenance shone with extraordinary royal dignity and moral authority.

The king frowned: 'Who are you, wandering mendicant, and what brings you to my throne?'

The youth answered: 'I was born Crown Prince of the great kingdom of Balkh. My father possessed armies twice the size of yours and treasuries overflowing with diamonds. Yet he governed with oppression and cruelty.

One day, an earthquake shook our capital; the palace collapsed, my father perished beneath his own golden throne, and our armies were scattered like dust. I walked through the smoking ruins of my ancestral home, and I realized that a throne built on tears is a house built on shifting sand. I renounced worldly power to warn the rulers of the earth:

"He who sows injustice shall reap the whirlwind; the sighs of the oppressed rise higher than the mountain crags, and their tears shall drown the mightiest empire!"'

The words struck the tyrannical king like a thunderbolt. He looked at the youthful prince who had renounced a crown for truth, and looked at his own trembling courtiers.

Profound shame and repentance pierced the king’s soul. He descended from his throne, embraced the pilgrim prince, ordered the immediate release of all prisoners, canceled unjust taxes, and restored confiscated lands, governing for the remainder of his days with justice and mercy.
moral: Earthly power that oppresses the weak is weighed by history and collapses into forgotten dust.
